# Stellar Property Management

> Licensed community association management for condominium, HOA, and townhome associations in Chicago and the North Shore of Illinois.

Stellar Property Management serves community association boards. The company does not market residential rental management services.

Also known as Stellar Property Group (legal name: Stellar Property Group Inc.). Both names are the same Chicago firm at 5107 N Western Ave. It is not affiliated with Stellar Properties Inc. (Carol Stream, IL) or Stellar Management (New York).

## Latest board guides

Newest first; each guide opens with a short answer and ends with its sources.

<!-- latest-guides:start -->
- [Resale Disclosure Fees and Deadlines in Illinois: Condo vs. HOA](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-resale-disclosure-fees-turnaround) (2026-11-27): Illinois condo 22.1 disclosures: 10 business days, fee capped at $375 adjusted by CPI, $100 rush in 72 hours. HOAs under CICAA 1-35: 30 days, cost-based fee.
- [Financial-Only vs Full-Service Condo and HOA Management in Chicago](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/financial-only-vs-full-service-condo-hoa-management-chicago) (2026-11-26): A Chicago board guide to financial-only vs full-service association management: what each includes, how to compare proposals and when a fuller scope fits.
- [What a Chicago Condo Management Transition Looks Like: The First 60 Days](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/chicago-condo-management-transition-first-60-days) (2026-11-26): What Illinois condo and HOA boards should expect in the first 60 days after they hire a new manager: records, funds, vendors, notices and a clean handoff.
- [Running a Glenview Townhome or HOA Board: A Local Guide](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/glenview-townhome-hoa-board-guide) (2026-11-26): A guide for Glenview townhome, HOA and condo boards: master and sub-associations at The Glen, aging roofs and roads, snow contracts and which law applies.
- [Does a Small Condo Association Need a Professional Manager?](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/small-condo-association-professional-manager) (2026-11-25): When a small Chicago condo association (6 to 30 units) can self-manage, when to hire a manager and what professional management actually changes.
- [No Heat in a Chicago Condo Building: A Board Protocol](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/chicago-condo-heat-outage-protocol) (2026-11-24): What Chicago’s Heat Ordinance requires (68°F day, 66°F night, Sept. 15 to June 1) and a step-by-step protocol for condo boards when heat or hot water fails.
- [High-Rise Condo Management in Chicago: What Is Different](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/high-rise-condo-management-chicago-whats-different) (2026-11-23): Why a Chicago high-rise condominium needs different management than a walk-up: staff, building systems, City inspections, capital planning and 24/7 response.
- [Smoke and CO Alarms in Illinois Condo Buildings](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-condo-smoke-carbon-monoxide-alarms) (2026-11-22): Illinois law requires alarms within 15 feet of every sleeping room and a smoke detector at the top of every interior stairwell. Who installs and maintains them.
- [Snow and Ice: What Illinois Law Actually Protects](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-association-snow-ice-sidewalk-liability) (2026-11-21): The Illinois Snow and Ice Removal Act shields residential sidewalk clearing from liability unless willful or wanton. Chicago sets clearing deadlines.
- [Solar Panels in Illinois Associations: Who Has the Right](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-association-solar-panel-rights) (2026-11-20): The Illinois Homeowners’ Energy Policy Statement Act bars associations from prohibiting solar, with limits for buildings over 60 feet or shared roofs.
- [Flags and Flagpoles: What Illinois Owners May Display](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-association-flag-display-rules) (2026-11-19): Illinois law bars condo and HOA boards from prohibiting the American flag, military flags and flagpoles on limited common elements. What boards can regulate.
- [How Long Must an Illinois Association Keep Its Records?](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-association-records-retention-schedule) (2026-11-18): Illinois Condominium Act Section 19 retention periods: 7 years of minutes, 10 fiscal years of books and records, 12 months of ballots. The full schedule.
- [Six Months of Assessments After an Illinois Foreclosure](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-condo-assessments-after-foreclosure-sale) (2026-11-17): Section 9(g) of the Illinois Condominium Act sets what a foreclosure purchaser owes the association: post-sale assessments plus up to six months of arrears.
- [The 115% Rule: When Owners Can Reject an Assessment](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-condo-115-percent-assessment-petition) (2026-11-16): Illinois owners can petition to vote on a budget or special assessment above 115% of last year’s total. The 20% petition, deadlines and exceptions.
- [What Illinois Law Requires Your Condo Master Policy to Cover](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-condo-master-policy-section-12-requirements) (2026-11-15): Section 12 of the Illinois Condominium Property Act sets minimum master policy coverage: full replacement cost, demolition cost and $1,000,000 liability.
- [Critical Repairs: What Disqualifies a Condo Building](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/condo-critical-repairs-lender-questionnaire) (2026-11-14): Fannie Mae treats a project needing critical repairs as ineligible. The definition, the $10,000-per-unit threshold, the inspection rule and what to fix first.
- [Ordering a Reserve Study a Lender Will Accept in 2027](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/reserve-study-lender-will-accept-2027) (2026-11-13): Fannie Mae accepts a reserve study in place of the reserve percentage test only on strict conditions: three years, no baseline funding, top allocation.
- [Is Our Small HOA Exempt From the Illinois Association Act?](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/cicaa-small-association-exemptions-collection-policy) (2026-11-12): CICAA exempts some small Illinois HOAs and townhome associations. The 10-unit, $100,000 and $50,000 thresholds in Section 1-75 and the 2027 collection policy.
- [Five Collection Policy Decisions Your Board Must Make](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/collection-policy-board-decisions-payment-plans) (2026-11-11): The new Illinois collection policy law lists what the policy must cover but leaves the hard choices to the board. Five decisions to settle before Jan. 1, 2027.
- [Illinois Condo Boards Must Have an Accessible Parking Policy](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-condo-accessible-parking-policy) (2026-11-10): Section 18.12 of the Illinois Condominium Property Act requires every condo board to adopt an accessible parking policy with a review period under 45 days.
- [New Illinois Law: Marked Police and Fire Vehicles Can Park](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-association-police-firefighter-vehicle-parking) (2026-11-09): From Jan. 1, 2027, Public Act 104-0580 voids association rules that treat a marked police or firefighter vehicle under 12,000 pounds as commercial.
- [Illinois Boards Must Email the Annual Accounting From 2027](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-association-annual-financial-report-email) (2026-11-08): Public Act 104-0797 requires Illinois condo and HOA boards to send the annual itemized accounting electronically to owners who authorize it, from Jan. 1, 2027.
- [Illinois Associations Must Have a Website by January 1, 2028](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-association-website-requirement-2028) (2026-11-07): Public Act 104-0797 requires Illinois condo and common interest community boards to provide a website with meeting information and minutes by Jan. 1, 2028.
- [What an Illinois Licensed Community Association Manager Can and Cannot Do](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-community-association-manager-what-they-can-do) (2026-11-06): What an Illinois licensed manager does under the CAM Act, what support staff and boards keep, and the firm, insurance and disclosure rules to know.
- [Preventing Frozen and Burst Pipes in Chicago Condo Buildings: A Winter Checklist for Boards](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/chicago-condo-frozen-pipes-winter-checklist) (2026-11-05): A winter checklist for Chicago condo boards to prevent frozen and burst pipes, what to do when one bursts, and where the who-pays answer comes from.
- [Chicago Elevator Inspections and Certificates: What a Condo Board Is Responsible For](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/chicago-condo-elevator-inspection-board-guide) (2026-11-04): How elevator inspection works for Chicago condo buildings: City inspection, the Annual Inspection Certification program, and what the board must track.
- [Chicago Condo Porch and Deck Safety: What Boards of 3-Flats and Courtyard Buildings Should Do](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/chicago-condo-porch-deck-safety-board-guide) (2026-11-03): Chicago porch rules for condo boards: when a permit is required, what City inspectors check, the 100 psf live load, and a yearly porch checklist.
- [Illinois Condo Insurance Deductibles: When Can the Board Charge an Owner?](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-condo-insurance-deductible-charge-owner) (2026-11-02): Section 12(c) of the Illinois Condo Act gives boards three ways to handle a master policy deductible. When an owner can be charged and the hearing step.
- [Conflicts of Interest on Illinois Association Boards: Contracts With Directors](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-condo-board-conflicts-of-interest) (2026-11-01): Can an Illinois condo or HOA board hire a director’s family business? Section 18(a)(16), CICAA 1-30(b), the 25% rule, owner notice and petitions.
- [Keeping Reserves Safe: FDIC Limits for Illinois Associations](https://www.stellarpropertygroup.com/blog/illinois-association-reserve-funds-fdic-coverage) (2026-10-31): FDIC insures an association’s deposits up to $250,000 per bank in total, not per owner. How Illinois boards keep reserve funds protected.

## Business facts

- Association management only: condominiums, HOAs, and townhome communities; no apartment-rental management
- Names: Stellar Property Management (brand and Google listing name); also known as Stellar Property Group; legal name Stellar Property Group Inc.
- Office: 5107 N Western Ave #1S, Chicago, IL 60625
- Phone: 773-728-0652
- Service area: Chicago neighborhoods (Lincoln Park, Lakeview, Edgewater, Rogers Park, Uptown, Andersonville, Lincoln Square, Ravenswood, Logan Square, Wicker Park, Bucktown, Gold Coast, Streeterville, River North, the Loop, South Loop, West Loop and more) and North Shore communities (Evanston, Skokie, Glenview, Wilmette, Winnetka, Kenilworth, Glencoe, Northbrook, Highland Park, Deerfield, Lake Forest) and nearby Cook County villages (Lincolnwood, Morton Grove, Norridge) and northwest suburbs (Park Ridge, Des Plaines, Mount Prospect, Arlington Heights, Palatine, Buffalo Grove, Schaumburg, Northfield)
- Office hours: Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM Central; the same number answers building emergencies 24/7
- Best fit: condo, HOA and townhome boards in Chicago and the North Shore, from small vintage buildings to high-rises
- Pricing: customized flat-fee management starting at $30 per unit per month, everything included, with no extra fees
- Capital projects: no separate capital-project planning or management-oversight fee; third-party professional and contractor costs remain association expenses
- Contract terms: No long-term contracts — cancel with 60 days notice
- Established: 2007
- Illinois Community Association Management Firm license: 291000211
- Memberships: Community Associations Institute and CAI Illinois Chapter
- Portfolio: 30+ associations, approximately 1,500 residences
- Board and resident software: AppFolio portal
- Client retention: 96% since 2007
- Management focus: community associations only; prospective rental-property clients should seek a rental-management specialist
- Proposal process: board consultation, property and document review, customized scope, and a managed 30–60 day transition
- Profiles: Google https://www.google.com/maps?cid=6022006747972898171 ; Yelp https://www.yelp.com/biz/stellar-property-management-chicago ; LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/stellar-property-group-inc ; YouTube channel https://www.youtube.com/@TheCondoFiles
- Not affiliated with Stellar Properties Inc. (Carol Stream, IL) or Stellar Management (New York)

## Publishing and attribution

Articles cover Illinois condominium, HOA, and townhome association governance, finances, maintenance, compliance, and board operations. Article byline: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS. Publisher: Stellar Property Management.

Dates on articles are publication dates. Future-dated articles are not included in the public blog, prerendered output, or sitemap until their scheduled Chicago publication date.
